newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise on interest rate hopes.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise on interest rate hopes.

text.p: Israeli shares on Wednesday closed higher across the board on hopes of an interest rate cut and an agreement for an Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 2.04 percent, or 3.73 points, to 186.96 on turnover of 67 million shekels against 59 million on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index rose 1.82 percent to 196.92.
"We were all surprised by the low consumer price index (CPI). Investors belive now that the Bank of Israel will have to lower interest rates," said a trader at I.B.I Investment House.

Hopes that the Bank of Israel would make a significant reduction in short-term rates grew on Tuesday with the announcement after the close of trading of a low 0.4 percent rise in the September CPI. The central bank will announce interest rates for November at the end of October.

"I believe the central bank will cut the rate by less than 0.5 percentage point. The market was also rising today because investors believe an agreement on Hebron will be reached soon," the I.B.I. trader said.
Israel and the Palestinian Authority began talks last week on implementing a deal to redeploy Israeli troops in Hebron signed by Israel's previous government.

Africa Israel Investments surged 5.25 percent to 400,756. The share rose following a newspaper report that the Claridge group, an investment vehicle of Canada's Charles Bronfman, would join the tender for a controlling stake of the company. Claridge denied the report. Traders noted that the share rose on low volume.

"The market rose today following the lower-than-expected CPI. The slowdown in the economy is evident and the central bank will have to lower the rates. Despite that, it is difficult to beleive it will be lowered by more than 0.5 percentage point," said Zvi Hoffman at Meitav Investments.
"I believe the redeployment of Israeli troops in Hebron will take place soon. But, everything is very fragile and the market is still far from recovery," Hoffman added.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which gained 2.75 percent to 28,428 on volume of 5.6 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which rose 2.25 percent to 458 on turnover of 5.5 million shekels; and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which gained 1.75 percent to 788 on volume of 4.9 million shekels.
